item.title: Navruz in the mahalla
item.context_text: It's March, and your mahalla is having a Navruz party in the courtyard. Your new neighbour, Emily, is from Canada and doesn't speak Uzbek yet. She wants to join in, so you help her in English.
item.objective_text: Understand the plan for the party, help Emily take part, and explain the holiday to her.
item.target_grammar: will and can for offers and plans (You can come later. We will start at 8.)
item.cultural_note: Navruz (21 March) is the spring new year in Uzbekistan and many other countries. Neighbours often cook sumalak together through the night and share it the next day.
success_conditions: Understand when things happen and what to bring
Answer Emily's questions about sumalak, time and food
Tell Emily two things people do at Navruz

children.title: Read the mahalla notice
children.instructions: The mahalla committee put this notice on the door in Uzbek, Russian and English. Read it and answer the questions.
children.prompt_text:
NAVRUZ IN OUR MAHALLA
21 March, from 10 am, in the courtyard behind Building 3.
We are cooking sumalak on the night of 20 March. Helpers are welcome from 8 pm!
Please bring a plate of food to share, or sweets for the children.
Music, games for children, and dancing at 4 pm.

questions.prompt: When does the cooking of sumalak start?
questions.explanation: "We are cooking sumalak on the night of 20 March. Helpers are welcome from 8 pm."
"Please bring a plate of food to share, or sweets for the children."

children.title: Listen to Emily
children.instructions: Emily sends you a voice message. Listen and answer the questions. You can listen again.
children.prompt_text: Hi, it's Emily from flat 12. I saw the notice, but I don't understand everything. What is sumalak? I'd like to help, but I work until seven on the twentieth. Can I come later? And what can I bring? I make really good apple pie.

questions.prompt: What time does Emily finish work on 20 March?
questions.explanation: "I work until seven on the twentieth."

children.title: Answer Emily
children.instructions: Write back to Emily. Explain what sumalak is in simple words, tell her she can come after work, and answer her question about food.
children.prompt_text: Emily: What is sumalak? Can I come after work? What can I bring?
children.goal: Explain sumalak, invite Emily to come later and answer her food question.
children.model_answer: Hi Emily! Sumalak is a sweet, traditional Navruz dish. We cook it from wheat in a very big pot all night. Yes, of course you can come later. We start at 8 pm and finish in the morning! Your apple pie is a great idea.

children.title: Explain Navruz
children.instructions: At the party, Emily asks you about the holiday. Tell her two things people do at Navruz.
children.prompt_text: Emily: This is fun! What do people usually do on Navruz?
children.goal: Tell Emily what people eat and one more Navruz tradition.
children.model_answer: We celebrate the new year and spring. People cook sumalak and halim, and they visit their family and friends. Children play games and everyone dances.
